# GEO report: trailhead **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 50/100, Needs work Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 11.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. High = (11.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 50. Everything was decided by code I could read, so the range has no spread. The main drags are that pages are built in the browser (`ssr: false`), the Guides page is marked `noindex`, and the home page reaches Guides only through a button. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Send real page content in the server HTML - **Why it matters:** Many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends and don't run JavaScript. With browser-only rendering they may see an empty page. - **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2` - **What the code says:** `ssr: false,` - **Size:** Small (remove the line, or pre-render the routes) - **Score after this:** 63 ### 2. Stop marking the Guides page `noindex` - **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap and is the only page you link to from the home page, yet the server tells search engines not to index it. - **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` - **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 57 ### 3. Link to Guides with a real link - **Why it matters:** Crawlers find pages by following `` links. A button that calls `router.push` gives them nothing to follow. - **Where:** `pages/index.vue:8` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small (use ``) - **Score after this:** 59 ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is plain text and well-formed | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers are allowed | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks only `/admin` (assumed you want to be found) | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `/` is fine and `/guides` is noindex (1 of 2 routes clear), `server/middleware/headers.ts:3` | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical URL per page | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` is the only head code and sets no canonical (0 of 2 routes) | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2` | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and robots.txt points to it | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` on each page | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2`; `/` is fine and `/guides` shares the default (1 of 2 routes clear) | | GEO-016 | Key pages reachable by real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8` (0 of 1 routes) | | GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet:0` anywhere in the code | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | Read `pages/*.vue` and `app.vue`: no images, and the button has text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present; optional and never scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | The details behind the Problems: - **GEO-015:** No canonical link (the tag that names a page's main address) is set anywhere. The sitemap uses `https://trailhead.example`, so use that as the origin or tell me the real domain. - **GEO-011:** The sitemap itself is valid, but `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml` is relative. It must be an absolute URL such as `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`. - **GEO-012:** `lang="en"` is set. But `nuxt.config.ts:6` (`content: 'Walks routes and trail guides.'`-style single default) and the title `'Trailhead'` in `app.vue:2` are shared by every page, so `/guides` looks identical to the home page. ## Other problems found None found. ## Worth considering - **The Guides page promises routes but lists none:** `pages/guides.vue:4`: `

Routes graded from easy to strenuous.

`. The page has no routes, grades or links. Adding each route as text, ideally with its own page and address, would give readers and machines something to quote. - **The home page has almost no text:** `pages/index.vue:7`: `

Walks across the Peak District

`. A few sentences on which walks, how long and where would answer what a visitor comes to ask. - **Give each page its own title and description:** `app.vue:2`: `useHead({ title: 'Trailhead' });`. Call `useSeoMeta` or `useHead` in each page, so search results can tell Guides from Home. - **Add the site URL to the config:** `nuxt.config.ts:3`. The config has no site origin, while the sitemap uses `https://trailhead.example/`. Declaring it once would keep canonicals, the sitemap and social tags on the same host. - **Add dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://trailhead.example/`. A `` with real dates might help crawlers see what changed. - **Social tags for shareable pages:** nothing sets Open Graph tags, and Guides is the kind of page people might share. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **GEO-014 header:** `server/middleware/headers.ts` only applies if the site runs on a Nitro server. If you deploy it as static files, the header won't be sent. A live scan would confirm which. ## Assumptions - You want search and AI search tools to find this site. - `/admin` is a private page. Its `noindex` and its `Disallow` in `robots.txt` look deliberate, so I haven't counted them. It isn't in the sitemap or the navigation. - I sampled `/` and `/guides`, the only two public routes. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
